title: Redbud, grown from buds
reads: At the page camera (ortho, turn 14, tilt 52): a loose, irregular dome of leaf clusters, a little taller than wide, on a short trunk that forks low and flares into the soil. Gaps between the clusters show dark limbs.
fits: Grown pieces: trees, shrubs and other branching plants whose limbs fork from a parent and whose leaves sit on shoots.
wrong_for: Hard-surface props, rigged characters, and anything whose shape is not a branching tree.

references.gives: 6-9 m tall, 8-10 m spread; "A 10-year-old tree will generally be around 5 m (16 ft) tall"; leaves alternate, heart-shaped, 7-12 cm; twigs "slender and zigzag, nearly black"; bark dark
20-30 ft tall, 25-35 ft wide; "Multi-stemmed", "Multi-trunked", "trunk usually divided close to ground"; stems "zig-zag, spreading and ascending"; bark dark brown to black
leaves "alternate", "light green on top, paler green underneath"
eastern redbud: "Terminal bud absent"; twigs "Slender, zigzag"
Owens & Ewers 1991, Can. J. Bot. 69: 1956-1963: vegetative buds are orthodistichous, each leaf about 180 degrees from the one below (also Owens 1990, MSc thesis, Michigan State)
leaf blade inclination, Cercis siliquastrum: mean 44.1 deg, SD 19.2, n 101 (Chianucci et al. 2018 data; beta fitted by the method of moments in a reference sweep)
Werner & Kenealy, USPP35080, Cercis canadensis 'NC2014-10' (a semi-compact cultivar), about 4 years old: height about 7.5 ft, width about 5 ft; internode 2.0 cm on average
Demol et al. lidar QSMs of beech and ash: first-order branches leave the stem at a median 44 to 54 degrees, and point 40 to 56 degrees from the zenith (other species, as read in a botany note)
summer: one leaning trunk about 15 cm across on a 5 m tree, forking low, flaring at the soil
heart leaves hanging on petioles about a third of the blade long, from zigzag twigs
